288785158_0bed7d98.text: In contrast, parvocellular PVN neurons exhibit greater functional and anatomical diversity. Neuroendocrine parvocellular neurons expressing corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) and thyrotropinreleasing hormone (TRH) project to the median eminence and regulate the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) and hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axes, respectively. These neurons are subject to extensive top-down modulation from limbic and cortical regions, rendering them particularly sensitive to chronic stress and affective states. Dysregulation of parvocellular CRH neurons represents a core mechanism underlying sustained HPA axis activation in stress-related disorders.
